subject: Follow-up: Private deployment hardware & offline ops — Genex Labs
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@genexlabs.com>, Michael Torres <michael.torres@genexlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Private deployment hardware & offline ops — Genex Labs

Hi Sarah / Michael —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on requirements for a Private (air-gapped) deployment at Genex Labs: 

Recap (from today’s discovery)
- Genex needs a fully offline / air-gapped deployment behind their internal firewall with no outbound internet from the inference appliance.
- Primary use: internal R&D workloads; target latency SLOs in the 200–500ms range for batched inference.
- Compliance: SOC2-aligned controls, on-prem key management, and audit logs retained for 12 months.

Open questions / action items (please confirm):
1) Rack & power: Can you confirm available rack U and per-rack power feed (208V/30A or 3-phase) for the initial 2-node cluster? Note: preliminary spec attached. [Attachment: redwood-private-hw-specs.pdf]
2) Upgrade windows: Are there maintenance blackout windows for firmware/patching? We need a twice-yearly planned maintenance window and a clearly defined emergency patch process for critical CVEs.
3) Spares & logistics: Will Genex provide onsite spares or should we include a spares kit in the BOM (PSUs, NVMe, power cables)?
4) Local IT & security: Confirm whether on-site IT must perform all network/physical access (no 3rd-party vendors allowed).

Proposed next steps:
- Genex to share rack/power drawing and list of requirements (target: by Tue, Mar 9).
- Redwood to prepare a short offline ops playbook and spares BOM for review.
- Book an on-site workshop during the week of Apr 11–15 for site survey and install planning (please flag any calendar conflicts).

I’ve attached the high-level HW spec and a short pre-deploy checklist to kick off the BOM and Ops playbook. If that looks good I’ll create a shared Drive folder with the SOW/DocuSign link.

Thanks — look forward to the details.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Dr. Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@genexlabs.com>

Cc: Michael Torres <michael.torres@genexlabs.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private deployment hardware & offline ops — Genex Labs

Thanks Ava — helpful summary. A few fast answers and clarifications below.

> On Fri, 05 Mar 2027, Ava Chen wrote:
> > Rack & power: Can you confirm available rack U and per-rack power feed (208V/30A or 3-phase) for the initial 2-node cluster?

We have two contiguous 2U slots in our main research rack (RACK-3). Power is 208V single-phase, breaker 30A per rack. I'll attach the rack drawing and power plan. [Attachment: facility-power-rack-drawing.pdf]

> > Upgrade windows: Are there maintenance blackout windows for firmware/patching?

We do have monthly maintenance windows — first Sunday 02:00–06:00 local time. For emergency security patches we can allow a 4-hour emergency window with prior notification + local IT present.

> > Spares & logistics

We can provide basic PSU spares but prefer Redwood include critical spares for GPU modules and NVMe. Please include recommended part numbers and lead times.

> > Local IT & security

All external vendor engineers must be escorted by our IT staff. No outbound internet is allowed from the appliance by default; we can provision a temporary RDP jump host during install under strict controls.

Next steps from our side:
- I will send the rack/power drawing by EOD today.
- I’ll coordinate with Facilities to flag Apr 11–15 as possible site survey dates; tentatively prefer Apr 12/13.

Thanks — happy to discuss the spares BOM once you send your recommendation.

—Sarah
Dr. Sarah Lin
Director, Computational Infrastructure
Genex Labs
sarah.lin@genexlabs.com | +1 (650) 555-4422
[Attachment: facility-power-rack-drawing.pdf]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Internal — quick notes based on Sarah’s reply and the spec: 

- Rack/power looks compatible with our 2U appliance (208V single-phase / 30A ok). We should still recommend a dual-cord PSU option for redundancy in the BOM.
- Spares: include 1 spare NVMe, 1 spare PSU, 1 spare NVLink cable (if applicable), and a replacement fan module. Estimate lead time 6–8 weeks for GPUs.
- Patching cadence: confirm with Product whether we can commit to a twice-yearly scheduled patch plus a critical emergency patch path that can be applied in the 4-hour emergency window Sarah mentioned. Need to flag any firmware that requires longer downtime.
- Doc ops: I’ll draft the spares BOM and a short offline ops playbook (roles: Genex IT for escorting, Redwood engineer for appliance service).

Ava — I’ll share the BOM draft in the Drive folder once we have Sarah’s drawing. Monica, please confirm if CS should lead the on-site workshop or if this is better handled by Solutions + Field Eng.

Thanks,
Ben
